analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy (16 November 2026)
key_insights: Last week's rates sell-off was the main market event. A stronger-than-expected US CPI print and hawkish Fed commentary pushed the 10yr Treasury yield up 27.9bps to 5.14%, its largest weekly rise since April 2025. The 2yr rose 33.0bps to 4.84%, its largest rise since October 2024.

Deutsche Bank's US economists revised their Fed call to three further 25bp hikes, in December, January and March. That takes the fed funds rate to 4.625% by the end of Q1 2027. The revision followed the hot CPI print.

Monthly core CPI was +0.30% against +0.2% expected. Governor Waller opened the door to a 50bps December hike, and markets priced +27bps of hikes for the December meeting (+7.2bps on the week). October PPI came in below expectations at +0.3% m/m versus +0.4% expected, and the 2yr yield pared back 3.8bps on Friday.

Nvidia reports tomorrow (Nov 17) and may outweigh everything else this week. It fell 12.75% last week, its largest weekly decline since April 2025, and led a late-week tech sell-off. The report calls it the print that will largely close out a bumper earnings season.

A tech sell-off is hurting Asia on Monday. TAIEX fell 5.74%, KOSPI 4.00% and Nikkei 2.09%. S&P 500 futures are down 0.49% and Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.00%, while European futures are flat. Hang Seng is up 0.84%.

China's October activity data showed weak domestic demand. Industrial production rose 4.8% YoY against 5.3% expected, retail sales rose 0.4% against 0.8% expected, and January-October fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% against an expected 7.0% decline. New home prices fell 0.15% m/m, with the pace of declines moderating.
Japan's Q3 GDP unexpectedly contracted by 0.1% YoY against +0.2% expected, and was flat q/q against +0.1% expected. The report attributes this to softer exports and weaker consumer spending.

US data this week: October retail sales and industrial production tomorrow, and housing starts, permits, pending home sales and the October FOMC minutes on Wednesday. DB economists expect headline retail sales unchanged, ex-autos +0.3% m/m, the control group +0.4% m/m and industrial production +0.3% m/m. The minutes pre-date the inflation surprise and risk looking stale.

12 Fed officials speak this week, and markets will look for evidence that the inflation surprise has shifted the Committee's reaction function. Fed Chair Warsh moderates a panel today in San Francisco as the first of five Fed task forces, on productivity and jobs, presents. DB's baseline is that it focuses on AI lifting productivity and growth without the same inflation pressure.

UK October CPI on Wednesday is expected at +3.80% YoY from +3.48%, with core at +2.87% from +2.78%. UK labour-market data are tomorrow, and UK retail sales, GfK confidence and the UK-EU summit are on Friday.
Japan October national CPI is due Friday. DB expects core to accelerate to +2.4% YoY from +2.1% and core-core to slow to +2.3% YoY.

Equity indices were mixed on the week. The S&P 500 gained 2.51% and the Nasdaq 2.27%, despite a Friday Nvidia-driven sell-off. The Philly semiconductor index rose 8.05% on the week but fell 3.43% on Friday. Stoxx 600 (+2.44%) and DAX (+3.60%) reached new highs, and the Nikkei rose 6.46%, the KOSPI 4.56% and the Hang Seng fell 3.45%.

The dollar index rose 1.09% on the week to its highest level since the April 2, 2025 tariff announcement. Gold posted its biggest weekly decline since June, down 4.58% to $3,884/oz. Bitcoin fell for a sixth consecutive week, down 12.24%.

European rates also sold off, with 10yr bund yields up 12.3bps, OATs up 16.5bps and BTPs up 9.4bps on the week. ECB hikes priced by next June rose 13.5bps to 59bps. Credit tightened in the risk-on mood, with US HY spreads 20bps tighter and EUR HY 25bps tighter, the latter the biggest tightening since April 2025.
Brent ended the week 2.52% lower at $95.84/bbl after a sizeable roundtrip. It traded below $90/bbl on Tuesday before hopes for an Iran resolution faded again.

The earnings calendar shifts to consumer and retail names. Home Depot, Disney and JD.com report Tuesday, Tencent, Palo Alto Networks, TJX, Lowe's and Target on Wednesday, and Walmart, Alibaba, PDD and Intuit on Thursday. The US retail names should give a read on the US consumer.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Tuesday Nov 17 (estimate-stage, no figures given in this note). The report says it may outweigh other events this week and will largely put a bow on the earnings season.

US consumer read this week from Home Depot (Tue), TJX, Lowe's and Target (Wed), and Walmart (Thu). Walt Disney and Palo Alto Networks are other US highlights. Alibaba, Tencent, JD.com and PDD report in China.

crypto_views: Bitcoin posted a sixth consecutive weekly decline (-12.24%), facing headwinds from higher rates and tech volatility.
risk_factors: Nvidia results tomorrow could drive the next move in tech after last week's late-week tech sell-off.
Persistent inflation upside could keep driving the rates sell-off, with 10yr Treasury yields at 5.14% and a possible 50bps December Fed hike.
Elevated borrowing costs weigh on housing.
Hopes for an Iran resolution fading again, with Brent still volatile.
Weak China domestic demand and the Japan GDP contraction.
The October FOMC minutes pre-date the inflation surprise, so they risk looking stale, and 12 Fed speakers may shift the reaction function.

Fed pricing: +27bps of hikes priced for the December meeting, and further Fed hikes priced for 2026 at 27 (-2bp on the day).
ECB hikes priced by next June rose +13.5bps to 59bps. iTraxx Crossover closed at 293 (+2).
US HY spreads tightened 20bps on the week and EUR HY spreads 25bps, the biggest EUR HY tightening since April 2025.
geopolitical: Hopes for an Iran resolution faded again last week, lifting Brent from below $90/bbl on Tuesday to end the week at $95.84/bbl.
APEC economic leaders' meeting in Shenzhen on Wednesday and Thursday adds a geopolitical angle to the week.
